claims.title: Exact Bellman recursion for fully observed finite law-state coding
claims.scope: finite rational source-law states, finite deterministic zero-error prefix-code actions, finite horizon, directed nonempty transition relation, and rational switching penalty
assumptions: the current law state is observed exactly before each code action
the adversary selects the next law after the current stage cost and code action
the first code action pays no switching penalty
nonclaims: the recursion does not apply unchanged when the current law is latent or estimated from finite samples
the finite transition relation is not a continuous-law control theorem

claims.title: Exact current-law observation cannot worsen the minimizing coder relative to open-loop commitment
claims.scope: the same finite law states, code actions, transition relation, switching penalty, initial state, and horizon under open-loop and fully observed policy classes
assumptions: a feedback policy may ignore observations and emulate any open-loop sequence
both games use the same adversarial transition timing
nonclaims: the value is not the value of one sample or one observed source symbol
a partial-observation policy need not attain the fully observed value

claims.title: Adversarial transition-set enlargement is monotone for open-loop and feedback coding values
claims.scope: two finite transition relations over identical law states where every successor set of the first is contained in the corresponding successor set of the second
assumptions: all code actions, costs, initial state, horizon, and information timing are held fixed
the source player maximizes cumulative expected length
nonclaims: transition-set inclusion is not inferred from data by this theorem
the monotonicity direction would reverse for a source player minimizing rather than maximizing cost

claims.title: Finite TV transition constructor is exact on the declared law-state set
claims.scope: a finite list of exact rational categorical laws and a rational total-variation transition threshold
assumptions: an edge i to j is allowed exactly when TV(q_i,q_j) is no larger than the threshold
the declared finite law list is the complete state space of the model
nonclaims: the finite relation is not an exact discretization of every law in a continuous TV ball
the threshold is a model parameter unless separately calibrated

claims.title: Mobile K3 exact feedback value and unit switching threshold
claims.scope: complete confusion on three symbols, point-mass law states with complete transitions, initial state e1, two periods, and complete binary prefix codes
assumptions: the current point-mass law is exactly observed before code selection
changing the short-leaf assignment incurs additive penalty kappa
nonclaims: the values V_OL=3 and V_FB=max(2+kappa, capped at 3) are specific to the declared finite instance
the example does not show that real source laws are observed exactly

claims.title: Bounded exact open-loop and observed-law Bellman audit
claims.scope: the finite K3, directed-transition, switching-threshold, monotonicity, and validation instances exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: the deterministic zero-error code universe and open-loop sequence space complete below configured caps
all value and policy tables are replayed over exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite agreement is not a scalability theorem
CI success does not make the finite game evidence for simulation
